For years, the HomePod mini has been my go-to speaker for everyday listening at home. It sounds great, looks sleek, and deeply integrates into the Apple ecosystem—all for just $99 (at least back I bought one when it launched). When Apple unveiled the HomePod mini 2 last week, I was tempted to replace my fully functional stereo pair solely to get the new software exclusives, such as Siri AI. That was until I installed the OS 27.2 update, which brings enough of the second-generation experience to the original HomePod mini to minimize my urge to upgrade.

Quite the glow-up

Sound Glow essentially brings the Dynamic Island’s animated waveform to the HomePod. The brand-new feature extracts the most prominent colors in a playing song’s album art and displays them on the HomePod’s touchscreen. The hues dynamically pulsate in sync with the track’s rhythm, reflecting the bass and treble in real time. While it technically doesn’t change how a song sounds, it does make the listening experience significantly more immersive and enjoyable.

I had assumed Apple would restrict Sound Glow to the HomePod mini 2, as my first-generation stereo pair is always within my sight when working, and such a feature would matter to me. The Music app on my Apple TV 4K 3 already provided a similar visualizer on the big screen; having my HomePod minis react with the same palette would contribute to the overall ambience.

I was pleasantly surprised to learn that Sound Glow is actually supported on all HomePods—excluding the original full-size model. After installing iOS 27.2 on my iPhone and its HomePod equivalent on my speakers, I was able to turn on and use Sound Glow on my 2020 minis just fine. Now they feel significantly more vibrant and energetic when blasting bops on them.

Mahmoud Itani / Foundry

Ghost buster

Many users have had to discard their otherwise functional HomePods because of the somewhat widespread phantom touch issue. The flaw repeatedly triggers the affected HomePod’s touchscreen without any user input, pausing/playing music and controlling the volume in a chaotic manner.

The latest OS update fixes the issue with a Lock Controls toggle in the Home app that optionally disables the touchscreen. So, whenever your HomePod starts misbehaving, you can kill touch input altogether and continue to rely on the otherwise functional speaker using voice commands or your iPhone.

Turning a blind AI

While OS 27.2 does not activate Siri AI on my original HomePod minis, the feature is arguably inessential in this context. The classic Siri generally works well for basic audio playback commands, and I tend to have longer, more complicated conversations with Siri AI using the keyboard on my iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Plus, the new HomePod mini 2 sells for $149, so upgrading my stereo pair would cost me another $300. It would make more sense to maintain my current HomePod setup and instead buy a HomeView for a similar price. This would unlock Siri AI and provide an always-on display as a bonus. Until Apple releases a meaningful upgrade, I will continue to rely on my trusty 6-year-old HomePod minis without a problem.

HomePod Software and iOS 27.2 will launch to the general public next week—potentially on Monday, October 26—with the Sound Glow and Lock Controls features. To try them early, you can sign up for Apple’s beta program and download the Release Candidate builds currently available.

OLED panels and ongoing supply-chain pressures could make the touchscreen models more expensive than today’s MacBook Pro, while touch support is expected to remain exclusive to Apple’s premium laptops initially. Read on for everything we know about the touchscreen MacBook Pro’s expected release date, design, specifications and price, including what Apple could announce on October 28.

Touchscreen MacBook Pro release date: When will it launch?

  • Apple media experience confirmed for October 28; touchscreen MacBook Pro announcement expected

The launch will reportedly include an online video presentation and an in-person component for the press on October 28. In his Power On podcast, Gurman said the laptop will start shipping on November 6.

Earlier reports offered a broader launch window and raised the possibility of delays. Speaking in a Power On podcast on October 1, Gurman said he expected the touchscreen MacBook announcement as early as October, potentially slipping to November. The laptops are reportedly being tested with macOS 27.2.

In September 2026, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman included the touchscreen MacBooks in a list of products that will ship in late 2026/early 2027.

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman and analyst Ming-Chi Kuo both initially predicted a late 2026 debut, with an October announcement fitting Apple’s traditional MacBook Pro release schedule while also coinciding with the 20th anniversary of the MacBook Pro’s introduction. In January, South Korean blog Naver reported that Samsung had begun production on its new 8.6-generation OLED manufacturing line, which is expected to supply panels for the next-generation MacBook Pro, further supporting that timeframe. Gurman also reported in February that the redesigned MacBook Pro would arrive in the “back half” of 2026.

Gurman’s more recent reporting points to an October announcement and November availability. However, the launch was previously predicted for early 2027. In April, Gurman reported that supply-chain constraints were affecting development of the redesigned MacBook Pro and could push the release into early 2027. He subsequently reported in June that Apple had revised its chip roadmap, with the touchscreen MacBook Pro now expected to launch with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips instead of M6 Pro and M6 Max in an effort to keep the project on schedule.

The feature is expected to debut on the high-end MacBook Pro models powered by Apple’s Pro and Max chips, making them the first Macs to support direct touch input.

Apple is expected to use the touchscreen as a key differentiator for its professional laptops, further separating the MacBook Pro from the more affordable MacBook Air and MacBook Neo.

There is also speculation that Apple could rebrand the flagship model as the MacBook Ultra. According to one report from a source said to be familiar with Apple’s plans, the company intends to expand its “Ultra” branding beyond the Mac Studio and Apple silicon chips. However, this claim has not been corroborated by Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman or analyst Ming-Chi Kuo, so it should be treated with caution.

For now, the technology appears set to remain exclusive to the MacBook Pro lineup. Neither the MacBook Air nor the MacBook Neo is expected to gain touchscreen support in the near term. However, Kuo believes Apple could eventually expand the technology to other MacBook models if the touchscreen MacBook Pro proves successful.

Foundry

One of the most significant visual changes could be the removal of the display notch. Reports from display analysts and Bloomberg suggest Apple may replace the current notch with a hole-punch camera cutout, allowing for more usable screen space around the sensor. In early 2026, Gurman went a step further, claiming the new MacBook Pro could adopt an iPhone-like Dynamic Island interface built around the camera cutout.

The touchscreen MacBook Pro is also expected to retain its traditional laptop design, complete with a full keyboard and large trackpad, rather than becoming a hybrid tablet device.

Other rumoured design changes include:

  • A lighter chassis, although the latest reporting suggests it may not be thinner.
  • OLED display technology.
  • A hole-punch FaceTime camera replacing the notch.
  • Possible Dynamic Island-style functionality.
  • A reinforced hinge designed to minimise screen movement when the display is touched.

These changes would help distinguish the MacBook Pro from the MacBook Air and the entry-level MacBook Neo while giving Apple’s flagship laptop its most substantial design update in years.

Which chip will feature in the touchscreen MacBook?

  • M5 Pro and M5 Max

The change could bring the M7 chips to market around six months earlier, with significantly improved on-device AI capabilities. The ongoing DRAM and NAND shortages may also have influenced Apple’s decision, although they are not thought to be the primary reason. Separately, Apple is reportedly planning to launch the 14-inch MacBook Pro with an M6 chip.

There has also been speculation that Apple could introduce its own 5G modem to a future MacBook Pro, enabling cellular connectivity without Wi-Fi or an iPhone hotspot. However, there is little concrete evidence that cellular connectivity will be part of the touchscreen redesign.

Touchscreen MacBook Display

  • Tandem OLED display
  • Touchscreen interface

The display is expected to be the headline upgrade of Apple’s redesigned MacBook Pro. Multiple reports suggest Apple will replace the current Liquid Retina XDR (mini-LED) panel with a touchscreen OLED display, bringing MacBook Pro technology closer to the Ultra Retina XDR display used in the latest iPad Pro.

According to analyst Ming-Chi Kuo, Apple is planning to introduce OLED touch panels in the MacBook Pro in late 2026 or early 2027. The new display is expected to be thinner, more power-efficient, and capable of delivering deeper blacks, higher contrast, richer colours, and improved HDR performance than today’s mini-LED screens.

Reports indicate that both the 14-inch and 16-inch models will use advanced tandem OLED technology, which combines two OLED layers to achieve higher brightness levels while maintaining excellent energy efficiency. Apple first introduced this technology with the M4 iPad Pro and is expected to bring a similar implementation to the MacBook Pro.

The touchscreen functionality will reportedly rely on on-cell touch technology, which integrates touch sensors directly into the display rather than adding a separate layer. This approach helps keep the panel thin while supporting multi-touch input.

If the rumours prove accurate, the move to a tandem OLED touchscreen would represent the biggest display upgrade in the MacBook Pro’s history and one of the most significant changes to the lineup in years.

Touchscreen MacBook Interface

Foundry

Rather than replacing the traditional desktop experience, Apple is reportedly working on a touch-tuned interface that adapts depending on how the device is being used. When touch input is detected, interface elements such as menus, buttons, and controls may automatically enlarge to make them easier to tap. When using a mouse or trackpad, macOS would revert to its familiar point-and-click layout.

The touchscreen itself is expected to support standard gestures such as tapping, scrolling, and zooming, while still allowing users to switch between touch, trackpad, and mouse input.

Further clues appeared in the macOS 27.2 beta on October 5. MacRumors reported new code references to touch gestures in Safari, Photos, Notes and Quick Look. These could support a future touchscreen MacBook, but they could also relate to Sidecar, which allows an iPad to act as a Mac display.

Apple

Reports suggest the company has explored bringing 5G connectivity to the MacBook lineup, allowing users to connect directly to mobile networks without relying on Wi-Fi or a smartphone hotspot.

In August 2025, Macworld reported that internal Apple code referenced a MacBook Pro with an M5 Pro chip and Apple’s C1 modem. This suggests Apple has experimented with cellular-equipped MacBooks, althogugh it does not establish that the upcoming touchscreen models will offer 5G.

The redesigned MacBook Pro could also benefit from Apple’s growing portfolio of wireless chips. The company’s N-series networking processors, which handle Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and Thread connectivity, may eventually replace third-party components throughout the Mac lineup. An updated version of the chip could debut alongside the touchscreen MacBook Pro, improving power efficiency and tighter integration with Apple’s ecosystem.

Apple will likely offer similar configurations to the current MacBook Pro models, but it’s unclear how much of a premium a touchscreen OLED display will command. Back in 2001, Steve Jobs introduced the concept of the Digital Hub, with a central device (the Mac) that “added value” to the other gadgets in our lives, including CD players, MP3 players, and cellphones. Very basic requests will be handled on-device. If the task is too big for your iPhone, it will send it to a Private Cloud Compute server along with the relevant data, where a much bigger processor and AI model can take care of it and then immediately delete everything associated with it.

Apple has been speaking about the benefits of local AI processing for quite some time now, but no phone or laptop is powerful enough for today’s best AI models, so it built a scheme to send AI requests from your iPhone or Mac to the cloud.

Now, the same principle is being extended in the other direction: Building “edge” accessories that do even less AI processing than your iPhone, but connect to it when they need to.

This allows Apple to build smaller, lighter, and relatively cheaper devices that can still access the company’s latest AI features. And it helps future-proof those devices as Siri AI evolves. It means your HomeView or AI-powered AirPods should get smarter as your iPhone gets smarter instead of being stuck with the limited AI processing available in a $299 smart display circa 2026.

Apple doesn’t directly tell us exactly how its products work, most of the time. But it’s a nice idea to think that you might update your iPhone in a few years, providing access to all new AI capabilities, and that your Apple Watch, HomeView, smart glasses, or other products will gain new capabilities in the process.

Is there any other company in the world whose followers obsess over how many units the company sells more than Apple? Maybe the Macalope’s wrong and somewhere out there are fans of the Hidden Valley Ranch company poring over rumors about the relative sales of Spicy Hot Honey versus Sizzlin’ Nashville Hot, or fret over rumors of devastating production cuts to the Creamy Jalapeño line, but he doubts it.

First of all, who doesn’t like Creamy Jalapeño? Why would there ever be production cuts to that line? It makes no sense.

iPhones, however, are different. Every year they get production cut rumors. And this year is no different: Apple cuts iPhone 18 Pro orders due to soft demand.

Nobody likes maroon. The Macalope could have told you that. It’s just a bad color.

This “news” comes from none other than Nikkei, purveyors of bombastic iPhone production cut rumors since 1973, a full three years before Apple was formed. No one had any idea what they were talking about for 34 years. Nikkei’s most garment-rending rendition was the 2017 iPhone X production cuts, which the outfit said were of such magnitude that Apple was producing negative iPhones, actually pulling already manufactured iPhones apart and putting the aluminum back into the ground.

Okay, not really, but it was wildly off, so take these reports with a salt-lick-sized grain of salt. It’s probably true that the price increase on the iPhone Pro line has not helped its attractiveness. Or maybe people were drawn to another, even more expensive option, because Apple apparently can’t make iPhone Duos fast enough.

Certainly not fast enough for Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, who said Apple made a “major mistake” with the iPhone Duo. What is this “major mistake’,” you may ask? Were credit cards charged twice? Thrice? Did every iPhone Duo ship with a dirty hypodermic needle in the box, just waiting to stab unsuspecting customers? Did some of the profits from each Duo go to a ridiculous vanity project, the real goal of which was to force companies to curry favor with a kleptocratic regime?

[Turns and stares unblinking into camera for 45 minutes]

Foundry

Well, according to Gurman, the “major mistake” was selling them before it had enough inventory to meet demand. Definitely an unprecedented event–or not: “iPhone 4 pre-orders from Apple now pushed back to July 14”.

Indeed, the Macalope himself vaguely recalls having to wait two months to get an iPhone 4 back in the day when the kids still said “back in the day.” Two months, of course, is not quite the three months would-be Duo owners have to wait now, but the iPhone 4 didn’t have an entirely new conceptual form factor, featuring a hinge and a foldable screen. All it had was a slightly janky antenna.

Was Gurman not able to get an iPhone Duo delivery date in 2026? Is that what this is about? Because as far as “major mistakes” go, selling as many as you can make seems a pretty great mistake to make.

Anyway, fear not, because Apple is on it: “Apple increases iPhone Duo orders by 30%“.

It is extremely unclear whether the current shortage is because of the unexpected popularity of the Duo or the relatively low number of units Apple was able to get built. Most likely a combination of both.

Apple sure picked a good year to move the base iPhone line to a spring release schedule, though: “IDC: Apple closes in on Samsung as global smartphone shipments see record decline in Q3”

Apple shipped fewer phones because it moved a whole line to spring. What’s your excuse?

The Macalope has always maintained that profit share is better than market share, but hey, if you can get both, so much the better.

Speaking of spring, get ready for a big one, at least sales-wise: “The standard version of the iPhone 18 is scheduled for production at the end of November, and the stock size seems quite large,” according to Fixed-Focus Digital, who has correctly reported Apple-related leaks in the past.

Year-over-year comparisons are going to be wack as the kids who used to say “back in the day” back in the day also used to say.

The Macalope realizes he’s putting a lot on these fictional kids of 2010, and he apologizes for any stress they may have incurred, temporal mechanically speaking.

The next year may make both Apple and its customers a little uneasy as the iPhone lineup gets rejiggered, but the Macalope suspects it’ll all work out in the end.

macOS 27 Golden Gate arrived on September 14, introducing an all-new Siri AI assistant, major updates to Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail and Calendar, and expanded child-safety features. Design refinements and performance improvements round out the release.

Named after California’s iconic Golden Gate, the update continues Apple’s push to make the Mac smarter and more proactive, bringing Apple Intelligence to more parts of the operating system to help users complete everyday tasks faster.

macOS 27 supports all Macs powered by Apple silicon, but drops support for Intel-based models. Intel Macs can continue running older versions of macOS, with security updates expected to remain available for a limited time.

This guide covers macOS 27’s biggest new features, compatible Macs and the latest beta developments. With some features still to come, we also explain what’s in the beta, what’s expected in future updates and when those additions could arrive.

What’s New in macOS 27 Golden Gate at a glance

Apple

Here are the top ten new features and changes in macOS 27 Golden Gate.

  1. Siri AI: A redesigned conversational Siri that can answer questions, understand personal and onscreen context, access the web and take actions across apps.
  2. Apple Intelligence: Systemwide proofreading, smarter writing tools, improved dictation and automatic file and folder naming.
  3. Safari upgrades: Automatic tab grouping, webpage change alerts with Notify Me, AI-generated extensions and faster, more efficient browsing.
  4. Smarter Messages and Mail: Better search and syncing, contextual suggestions and improved reliability.
  5. New Photos tools: Spatial Reframing, image expansion with Extend, improved Clean Up, and better search and organization.
  6. More powerful built-in apps: New features for Passwords, Calendar, Notes, Preview, Freeform, Weather, Shortcuts, and Image Playground.
  7. Expanded parental controls: Ask to Browse, improved Screen Time, contact approvals and broader Communication Safety protections.
  8. Better Mac gaming: Game Porting Toolkit 4 promises significant performance and compatibility improvements for Windows games.
  9. Refined Liquid Glass design: Better readability and consistency, adjustable transparency, cleaner Finder windows, and improved iPhone Mirroring.
  10. Faster macOS performance: Quicker app launches, Spotlight, AirDrop and networking, plus improved external-display, Thunderbolt and Bluetooth support.

macOS 27 latest version: What’s in macOS 27.0.1

macOS 27 became available to install on compatible Macs on September 14.

Apple then released the macOS 27.0.1 update on September 28, 2026. According to Apple’s security releases document, ” “This update has no published CVE entries.”

macOS 27.2, is currently in beta so that may be the next version of macOS 27. We don’t know if that means Apple will skip macOS 27.1. With iOS 27.1 being released for the iPhone Duo – with features specifically designed for the foldable – it is possible that Apple will move straight to macOS 27.2 in order to keep the version numbers in alignment. Alternatively, there may be secret features coming to the Mac in macOS 27.1.

Latest macOS 27 Beta – What’s coming in macOS 27.2?

Apple

Apple released the first developer beta of macOS 27.2 on September 16, followed by beta 2 on September 21, beta 3 on October 5 and beta 4 on October 13.

The macOS 27.2 release candidate arrived for developers on October 19. A release candidate is a build intended for final testing before general release so the non-beta version is expected soon.

Apple lists iOS 27.2 or iPadOS 27.2 as a requirement for setting up HomeView, which goes on sale on November 13, which could indicate a similar release date for macOS 27.2 since Apple usually issues software updates in tandem.

Apple has not announced any major additions coming with macOS 27.2, but clues appeared in the macOS 27.2 beta on October 5. MacRumors reported new code references to touch gestures in Safari, Photos, Notes and Quick Look. These could support a future touchscreen MacBook, but they could also relate to Sidecar, which allows an iPad to act as a Mac display.

Further clues emerged in October. As we reported on October 15, footage shared by itspdfu reportedly shows touch-oriented changes to Safari in macOS 27.2 betas 3 and 4. When rearranging tabs, the selected tab lifts and enlarges as it moves, then returns to its normal size when dropped into place. Pressing and holding a tab also opens a contextual menu, but this version omits the Ask Siri option available when using a mouse or trackpad. These changes suggest Apple is exploring how Safari could respond to touch input.

Apple has announced additional Siri AI languages for October, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish.

Automatic password changes and SynthID identification for AI-generated images remain forthcoming features. Their inclusion in macOS 27.2 has not been verified though.

Want to run te beta? Here’s how you can participate in the beta program we also recommend reading our guide to whether you should install the latest macOS beta. Beta software can cause crashes, app compatibility problems, increased battery drain and, in some cases, data loss. If you install a beta, make a full backup first and, ideally, use a secondary Mac, separate volume or external SSD.

What features are still to come in macOS 27

At the time of the launch of macOS 27 not all of Apple’s promised features were available. Missing features include:

  • Automatic password changes: The ability for the Passwords app to visit supported websites and automatically replace compromised passwords was removed shortly before release. 
  • Additional Siri AI languages: Siri AI launched in English only. French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish are due in October. 
  • SynthID identification for AI images: Apple said support for adding SynthID identification to most AI-generated or edited images would arrive in a software update later in 2026. 

macOS 27 problems: Are there any issues with Golden Gate?

Since macOS 27 Golden Gate arrived on Macs there have been reports in the Apple Support Community of issues with Mission Control and Spaces.

These include:

  • Stuttering or delayed transitions: Reports long pauses before a new Space appears.
  • Black or missing desktop previews: A black screen may appear when switching Spaces.

French website MacGeneration was able to reproduce some Mission Control glitches.

It is likely Apple will address these issues in macOS 27.2, if not before.

Siri AI: Siri powered macOS 27 features

Foundry

Apple’s biggest focus in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Siri AI, a completely redesigned version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence. Rather than functioning primarily as a voice assistant, Siri is now a conversational AI that can answer questions, understand personal and onscreen context, access current information from the web and take actions across apps.

Siri AI behaves more like a generative-AI chatbot than the Siri of old. It can answer questions directly, understand natural follow-ups and solve problems instead of simply directing users to web searches.

At a glance: What’s new with Siri AI?

  • Conversational AI assistant: Siri can handle open-ended questions, brainstorming, research and natural back-and-forth conversations.
  • Dedicated Siri app: A standalone Siri app keeps conversations in one place and syncs them through iCloud, allowing users to start a conversation on one Apple device and continue it on another.
  • Personal context awareness: Siri can understand information in Messages, Mail, Notes, Photos, Maps and files to locate information and provide answers based on your personal data.
  • Web-powered answers: Siri can access current information from the web, making it more useful for research, learning, interview preparation and questions about recent events.
  • App actions and automation: Siri can perform tasks across apps such as Messages, Music, Reminders, Calendar and Maps using natural-language instructions.
  • Spotlight integration: Siri AI is integrated with Spotlight, allowing users to type questions and receive AI-generated answers without opening a browser or separate app.
  • Visual Intelligence: Visual Intelligence comes to the Mac for the first time, allowing Siri to understand selected images, documents, files, text and other content displayed on screen.

Macwelt

  • Writing Tools: Siri can generate text, rewrite drafts, summarise content and adjust wording or tone. Apple says it can also adapt writing to the way you typically communicate with particular contacts.
  • Improved dictation: Systemwide dictation gains better speech recognition along with automatic punctuation, capitalization and formatting.
  • Custom Siri voices: Users can choose Siri’s voice and adjust characteristics such as pace and expressiveness, although some of these capabilities require newer hardware.

A Siri AI contextural popover was discovered during beta testing. Selecting text brings up a small Siri icon offering contextual actions, including Writing Tools, summaries and key points, sending messages or emails, creating calendar events, opening locations in Maps, and tracking flights or packages. However, the feature is not enabled by default and requires Apple’s FeatureFlags system to activate. It remains unclear whether Apple intends to make it available as a consumer-facing feature.

Apple also appears to be taking a relatively restrained approach to AI behaviour. In our testing, Siri avoids presenting itself as human, excessive flattery and potentially harmful responses, while generally keeping its answers straightforward.

Siri AI has launched as a beta, so users should expect some rough edges and continued improvements.

Siri AI initially supports English, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish due in October. Availability will vary by region. Siri AI is available on Mac and Vision Pro in the European Union, although Siri AI remains unavailable on iPhone and iPad in the EU at launch because of issues related to the Digital Markets Act. It is also unavailable in mainland China while Apple works through regulatory requirements.

Which Macs support Siri AI?

Siri AI requires a Mac that supports Apple Intelligence, but some of its most advanced capabilities have higher hardware requirements. Apple says its most powerful on-device AI model, expressive Siri voices and advanced dictation require an M3 or later Mac with at least 12GB of unified memory. Macs that support Apple Intelligence but do not meet those requirements can still receive other Siri AI features, although the exact feature set may vary.

Safari features in macOS 27

Apple

Safari gets several Apple Intelligence-powered upgrades in macOS 27, including smarter tab organization, webpage monitoring, custom extension generation, and performance improvements.

  • Automatic Tab Topics: Safari automatically groups related tabs by topic as you browse, helping keep research and projects organized. These groups can also be saved for later.
  • Notify Me: Safari can monitor webpages for changes and alert you when something happens, such as a product coming back in stock or a price dropping, removing the need to keep refreshing pages manually.
  • Describe an Extension: Users can create custom Safari extensions simply by describing what they want. Safari generates the extension from the text description and add it to the toolbar.
  • Faster, more efficient browsing: Apple says Safari uses less power while improving page-loading speed, JavaScript performance, scrolling, animations and resizing of the Start Page.

Messages and Mail features in macOS 27

Messages and Mail gain deeper Apple Intelligence integration in macOS 27, alongside improvements to search, syncing and everyday reliability.

Messages

  • One-Tap Suggestions in Messages: Messages suggests useful actions based on the context of a conversation, such as creating a reminder or note without leaving the chat.
  • Smarter Photo Suggestions: Messages surfaces relevant photos based on people, places and keywords mentioned in a conversation.
  • Personalized Smart Reply: During the preview at WWDC Apple indicated that suggested replies can reflect your usual writing style and adapt depending on who you’re messaging. This was removed from the iOS 27 beta before launch and hasn’t arrived with macOS 27.

Mail

  • Personalized Smart Reply: Apple also previewed a feature in Mail whereby it could generates suggested responses that better match your writing style and the person you’re replying to, but this is absent from the first version of macOS 27.

Photos has new AI-powered editing and organization tools in macOS 27, making it easier to improve images, find photos and manage an iCloud library.

  • Spatial Reframing: Photos will intelligently recompose and reframe images after they’ve been taken.
  • Extend Tool: A new Extend tool can expand an image beyond its original boundaries, filling in missing areas when changing the crop or aspect ratio.
  • Enhanced Clean Up: Apple’s Clean Up tool is better at removing larger unwanted objects and distractions from photos.
  • Better organisation and search: Photos adds keywords, star ratings, improved metadata search and other tools for organising a library.

macOS 27 also brings a wide range of smaller upgrades across Apple’s built-in apps, with a particular focus on automation, organisation, security and Apple Intelligence.

Passwords

In macOS 27 the Passwords app will automatically identify weak or compromised passwords and, with Apple Intelligence, visit supported websites, change the password and save the new credentials. This could remove much of the manual work involved in updating large numbers of old or leaked passwords, although questions remain over website compatibility, two-factor authentication and how consistently the feature will work.
